lens: SECLUSION — maximize beautiful stops with literally nobody around on Monday afternoon 7/6, plus a private mountaintop/lakeside sit-and-stare spot; crowded famous stops count against
ranking: Jocassee Gorges + NC-215 barbell to the Highland Scenic Highway (Elkins WV)
Foothills Waterfall Country -> NC-215 -> Goshen Pass -> Monterey -> US-250 Shenandoah Mountain (Staunton VA)
Cherokee Foothills–Big Walker–High Plateau run to PA-144/Hyner View (Mill Hall PA)
reasoning:
1) WV-150/Elkins is the purest seclusion play in the field. It stacks the most literally-nobody-there stops of any candidate, concentrated in the golden-hour window when they matter: Salmon Run boat launch at 5:45pm is a near-perfect recreation of the driver's beloved deserted Hartwell dock (paved dead-end ramp into 45-ft-visibility water, reviewers explicitly say weekday/off-hours = empty); Falls of Hills Creek at 0-2 cars; the FR-102 bog spur that 'connects nothing to nothing'; then 23 miles of commercial-vehicle-banned parkway where a blogger seeking solitude found ONE other car — and Red Lick Overlook alone at 8:45pm sunset is the exact private-mountaintop smoke spot requested. It uniquely delivers BOTH the lakeside and the mountaintop sit-and-stare in one evening, in the National Radio Quiet Zone fringe where emptiness is structural, not luck. Its only crowd exposure (Whitewater Falls) is timed to 10am Monday when reviewers confirm it's light, and the NRG Bridge stop is explicitly skippable. Under this lens the 11.5h length and the mediocre HIE hotel are irrelevant; the crowdRisk write-up ('lowest of any Mid-Atlantic corridor') is credible because the geography backs it — Pocahontas County has no services, no cell, and no through-traffic.

2) Goshen Pass/US-250/Staunton wins second on breadth and reliability of emptiness. The entire post-Lexington evening runs through Bath and Highland counties (~2,200 and ~2,800 residents) — a chain of nobody-there spots rather than one finale: unmarked Goshen Pass turnouts over the Maury on a Monday evening after swimmers leave, Hidden Valley's dead-end mansion meadow, the paved Blue Grass 'Switzerland' farm lane at dusk with likely zero other cars, Braley Pond as a park-facing-the-water bonus, and Confederate Breastworks as a drive-up summit sunset the driver will almost certainly have alone (TripAdvisor notes no cell coverage — i.e., nobody goes). Crucially it's more RELIABLE than the tighter-margin finales elsewhere: the sunset stop arrives ~8:00pm with slack, and its only famous stop (Whitewater Falls) is hit at 10am. Slight deductions vs #1: the private-water moment (Braley Pond, short gravel) is weaker than Salmon Run, and the BRP Black Balsam zone is a midday drive-through past hiker cars.

3) The Hyner View/PA-144 corridor takes third because when it's empty, it's the emptiest ground in the East: Fish Dam and Two Rock Run vistas face a literally roadless Wild Area (pure park-nose-out-and-shut-it-off), reviewers say midweek you get the entire Hyner terrace to yourself 1,300 ft over the Susquehanna, and Kettle Creek is 'no traffic, no planes.' Zero genuinely crowded stops all day (Big Walker is a small flex stop, not a strip). What keeps it behind the top two under a *reliability* lens: the seclusion is all bookended into the final 90 minutes after 5.5h of interstate, the Monday-AFTERNOON-spots requirement is thin (the afternoon is I-81/I-70), and the sunset margin at Hyner is razor-thin — one truck backup and the private-mountaintop payoff degrades to blue hour. Near-misses: Spruce Knob/US-33 has arguably the single best private summit but fewer secluded spots and a famous crowd-gamble (Looking Glass Falls) mid-route; Burkes Garden is wonderfully deserted but its headline road (VA-16) is a motorcycle pilgrimage even midweek; the Cherohala corridor, though empty by traffic counts, routes through the Highlands tourist mile, a newly-reopened high-visitation Bald River Falls, and a Look Rock sunset that draws company — three lens violations the top three avoid.

lens: DRIVE-EXPERIENCE: pavement quality, sweeper/switchback suitability for a heavy powerful luxury sedan, scenic density per mile, joy-to-slog ratio, and timing honesty
ranking: Waterfall-to-Skyway Grand Corridor (Wayah Rd -> Cherohala Skyway -> Foothills Parkway West -> Maryville/Alcoa TN)
Waterfall-to-Dragon corridor (US-276/BRP -> VA-16 Back of the Dragon -> Burkes Garden -> Wytheville VA)
Foothills Waterfall Country -> NC-215 -> Goshen Pass -> US-250 over Shenandoah Mountain -> Staunton VA
reasoning:
Judged purely on what happens through the windshield and under the tires, the field splits cleanly into routes that ARE the drive and routes that BUY a drive with hours of slab.

#1 Waterfall-to-Skyway (Maryville/Alcoa) is the runaway winner on every lens criterion. Pavement: the Cherohala is Hagerty's 2025 Road of the Year — 43 miles of billiard-smooth asphalt cresting 5,390 ft, exactly the wide, banked, high-speed sweeper geometry where a long-wheelbase 7 Series M Sport is at its absolute best (unlike the cramped 2nd-gear Dragon, which this route wisely skips). Foothills Parkway West adds 33 miles of fresh NPS asphalt including the 2018 'missing link,' and Wayah Rd's 28 recently-repaved forest S-curves are the bonus third act nobody knows about. Joy ratio: this is the ONLY corridor with essentially zero interstate — nearly all 8.7 driving hours are on roads you'd drive for their own sake, versus 4-5.5 hours of I-81/I-77 slab tax on almost every competitor. Scenic density per mile is the highest of the eight: waterfall, gorge, lake, mile-high crest, and Smokies sunset stacked continuously. Timing honesty: 8.7h driving / ~12h door-to-door with a 9:15pm arrival is the only itinerary comfortably UNDER the 10h core target with real slack for thunderstorm delays — every claim checks out against mountain-mile realities. Only demerits: gravel-on-apex caution on Wayah's final climb and 30 touristy minutes near Highlands, both engineered as pass-throughs.

#2 Waterfall-to-Dragon (Wytheville) is the best pure driver's-road day after the Cherohala route. VA-16's 32 freshly repaved miles and 400+ curves over three summits mix 55-mph sweepers with signed 15-25 mph hairpins — demanding but rewarding in a big sedan on new pavement — and the VA-623 climb into Burkes Garden adds documented NEW pavement switchbacks with a free second run on the backtrack. Interstate content is the second-lowest (~2h15, and the I-26 Sam's Gap portion is genuinely scenic), so the joy ratio is strong. Timing is honest: 9.8h driving, ~12h door-to-door, 9:15pm arrival with trimming levers identified. It loses to #1 on scenic density (pastoral 8.5, no continuous mile-high crest), on the mid-corner motorcycle risk on VA-16, and because hitting the Dragon at ~4pm sits squarely in the July pop-up storm window — blind 15-mph corners in rain in a 4,400-lb sedan demand restraint that dilutes the payoff.

#3 goes to the Staunton corridor on pavement-quality evidence the others can't match for their finales: US-250's curves are documented as paved extra-wide and nicely banked for logging trucks, 'in very good condition over the entire distance' with extremely light traffic — tailor-made 7 Series geometry — and the morning NC-215 Forest Heritage climb (17 miles of banked switchbacks, near-zero traffic) is arguably the best opening road of any candidate. Goshen Pass river curves and VA-42 make even the connector miles pleasant. The penalty is the honest ~4.5-hour I-26/I-81 midsection (the worst joy ratio of my top three), but timing is truthful at ~12-12.5h with a 9:15pm arrival and named pressure-release valves. It edges out the two Elkins routes and Reddish Knob because: the Highland Scenic Highway day runs 13.5h with an 80-minute full-dark deer-corridor finale (timing at the ceiling's edge, joy spent in darkness); the Spruce Knob route ends on a narrow, pothole-reported, blind-curve forest road descended in the dark — a pavement-quality fail for this car; Reddish Knob's FR-85 is one-lane and pothole-dotted at the summit; and the PA-144/Hyner run is 12.5h of driving with 5.5 hours of truck-choked I-81/I-70, the worst joy-to-slog ratio in the field despite a superb final 90 minutes. The Kentucky corridor's potholed-gravel arch finale and 8/8 road scores never seriously contended on this lens.

ranking: Waterfall-to-Skyway Grand Corridor: Seneca SC → SC 130/NC 281 (Upper Whitewater Falls) → US 64 Cullasaja Gorge waterfall mile (Bridal Veil drive-up) → Franklin → Wayah Rd (NC 1310) along the Nantahala cascades and Nantahala Lake → Robbinsville/Santeetlah Gap → Cherohala Skyway (43 mi, mile-high sweepers) with Indian Boundary Lake side spur → Bald River Falls out-and-back on Tellico River Rd → TN 360 valley run → US 129 along Chilhowee Lake → Foothills Parkway West sunset finale at Look Rock → Maryville/Alcoa TN

Waterfall-to-Dragon corridor: Seneca SC → SC-130/NC-281 (Upper Whitewater Falls) → US-64 → Brevard → US-276 through Pisgah (Looking Glass Falls) → Blue Ridge Parkway MP 412→393 (Pounding Mill / Looking Glass Rock overlooks) → I-26 over Sam's Gap → I-81 → Marion VA → VA-16 'Back of the Dragon' 32 mi/400+ curves → Tazewell → VA-61/VA-623 paved switchbacks into Burkes Garden crater valley → backtrack VA-623 → VA-61 Clear Fork valley → Rocky Gap → I-77 (or US-52 Big Walker sunset option) → Wytheville VA

Foothills Waterfall Country -> NC-215 Forest Heritage Byway over the Blue Ridge crest -> I-26/I-81 transit -> Goshen Pass -> Warm Springs -> US-220 Jackson River valley -> Monterey -> US-250 over Shenandoah Mountain into Staunton
reasoning: Judged purely on practicality — hotel fit, July weather exposure, logistics, closure risk, and stress-free day flow. #1 Waterfall-to-Skyway (Maryville/Alcoa): the only corridor under the 10h core target (8.7h), landing at 9:15pm at the field's best hotel cluster — a 2020 Courtyard, Tru, and Home2 with free surface lots in an airport submarket where night-of Monday booking after July 4th is essentially guaranteed at $115-190. Weather-wise the mile-high Cherohala crest is the midday heat escape, storms there mean 20-min view pauses rather than a lost finale, and there's a clean 75-min bail-out (US 411 direct) if running late. Fuel logistics are simple and known (Franklin/Robbinsville). Its crowd pinch points (Highlands, Bald River) are engineered as pass-throughs. #2 Back of the Dragon (Wytheville): 9.8h with a 9:15pm arrival, and the cheapest sure-thing hotel outcome anywhere — Tru (~2020 build) at $116 plus Fairfield and Hampton fallbacks, all interstate-exit surface lots with near-zero walk-in risk. VA-16 was fully repaved (low closure risk), Burkes Garden's paved-in/paved-out plan respects the 7 Series, and the sunset stop is optional rather than load-bearing, so a 4pm thunderstorm degrades the day gracefully. Only demerits: the Marion food/fuel hard gate and pastoral (8.5) scenery. #3 Staunton via US-250: 10.7h but a civilized 9:00-9:15pm arrival at a 2020 Tru (~$115-150) with a Fairfield for the Marriott preference in a cheap, soft post-holiday market. The Confederate Breastworks finale is a drive-up lot on a through road — no dead-end one-lane to descend in the dark — so weather or delay costs a view, not safety margin. It edges out the otherwise-similar Reddish Knob/Harrisonburg corridor (better hotel, Home2 May 2025) because that route's sunset math is minutes-thin and ends with 7 miles of one-lane FR-85 in the dark — built-in stress. The Elkins pair (WV-150, Spruce Knob) and Hyner PA all fail practically: 11-12.5h drives, 10:30pm+ arrivals, no 2019+ hotels, long dark deer corridors, cell dead zones, and zero weather slack. Kentucky/Creelsboro fails on July heat (~90F at the river at 7pm) and a potholed-gravel-plus-ladder headline stop that violates both the sedan and minimal-walking rules.
